supersedes: No prior capture or public-CLI settings contract; this adds one bounded OS lifecycle recovery for the existing unregistered host.
observed_problem: The original2.9.1 unregistered PuriPuly process PID57448 remains alive while supported app discovery/status expose no controllable instance for it. The CLI owner found no public attach/register-existing or PID-targeted normal-close command. A new lease-guarded GUI host is controllable through the supported CLI.
decision: Permit one documented Windows Process.CloseMainWindow request from PowerShell CLI to the exact existing PID57448, only after fresh executable-path/hash and creation-time identity checks against the retained intake record. This is normal close, not forced process termination, native GUI interaction, or private PuriPuly IPC.
before_close: Normally stop and exit the newly CLI-owned host first through the supported PuriPuly CLI, so old-host shutdown cannot race its settings writes or capture. Preserve both lifecycle records and the canonical ownership journal.

owned_host_shutdown_extension.reason: Supported capture stop succeeded OFF with owned resources released; public app stop returned exit7 unknown_execution for operation e8d701953b0b4b98b28ac7eccf8a98b7. Later discovery returned instance_not_found while the exact owned process remained alive after a bounded15s wait.
owned_host_shutdown_extension.permission: Permit one identity-guarded documented Process.CloseMainWindow request through PowerShell CLI for owned3708 before attempting57448. The same finite-exit/no-force/no-private-IPC rules apply. Preserve the original public-CLI shutdown failure separately; this extension does not turn it into a successful CLI exit.
owned_host_shutdown_extension.gate: Proceed to57448 only after actual3708 exit; otherwise report the bounded normal-close failure without expanding targets or repeatedly retrying.

hidden_window_extension.reason: MainWindowHandle=0 excluded the actual hidden top-level Flutter window; the exact original process has no descendants. The packaged normal CLOSE handler hides the window, awaits lifecycle shutdown and destroys it.
hidden_window_extension.permission: Director may send one standard WM_CLOSE through bounded SendMessageTimeoutW from PowerShell CLI to this exact hidden root window after fresh executable path/hash, process creation time, HWND owner PID/thread/class and top-level ownership validation. This replaces only the no-main-window stop for this newly evidenced target.
hidden_window_extension.bounds: Message timeout2s; actual process-exit observation at most60s. No show/restore/activation, broadcast, WM_QUIT, DestroyWindow, private IPC, process-force termination or new target. Preserve the previous no-main-window result and every new return/error/exit observation.

target_scope: The owner-existing process is adopted only for this explicitly bounded normal-close recovery. Do not retroactively claim it was benchmark-owned or that its effective routing/capture state was observed.
result_gate: Observe actual exit with a finite bound; command acceptance or a disappearing window is not whole-process closure. If identity does not match, no main window exists, close is refused, or it remains alive, preserve the outcome and stop this close path. Do not substitute another PID, kill/force termination, synthesize OS shutdown, or invoke hidden app commands.
after_close: Only after confirmed old-host exit, launch a fresh original-config GUI host through documented run-gui, verify actual build/instance/guarded effective state and applicable source admission, then prepare continuation under a new freeze. Settings and measurement lifecycle remain on the supported PuriPuly CLI.
preservation: No completed or first-product-failed main replay
Original PP4D3 raw chunks and mixed-route failure evidence retained
No settings/secret clones or direct live settings rewrite
No new service, account, model or tier
No game inspection/control or presence notes
No forced termination or remote publication
execution_status: Authorization and decision only; no legacy-host closure is claimed here.
